3.definition: (informal) To add; to subject to addition.
3.example: For him y is a unique number, like 7, but for the time being unknown — if one does the operation of 'plussing 4' one still has, as a result, a unique number even though one does not yet know what it is.

3.definition: (often, followed by ‘up’) To increase in magnitude.

3.definition: To improve.
3.example: Coach Wooden didn't have to depend upon having the most talented players on his team because he could depend upon plussing to constantly make everyone better.

3.definition: To provide critical feedback by giving suggestions for improvement rather than criticisms.
3.example: The animators and directors on the receiving end of the plussing don't necessarily have to accept and incorporate the feedback, but plussing provides a method to share criticisms in a way that makes it more likely that they will.

3.definition: (sales) To sell additional related items with an original purchase.
3.example: Good will is also secured by plussing the original purchase with another article that goes appropriately with it.

3.definition: To frame in a positive light; to provide a sympathetic interpretation.
3.example: Plussing is a technique for enhancing a positive atmosphere in the session, for diminishing hostility, and for raising self-esteem.

3.definition: (social media, dated) To give a mark of approval on Google+.

3.definition: To increase the potency of a remedy by diluting it in water and stirring.

3.definition: To increase a correction.

active_cells.definition: (colloquial) Used in phrases with existential there (also here and where) when the semantic subject is plural.
active_cells.example: There is three of them there.

active_cells.definition: (dialectal, form-of, indicative, present) present indicative of be; am, are, is.
active_cells.example: Let the whole world know we's on some off-key tip

active_cells.definition: And; sum of the previous one and the following one.
active_cells.example: Two plus two equals four.

active_cells.definition: (colloquial) With; having in addition.
active_cells.example: I've won a holiday to France plus five hundred euros in spending money!

active_cells.definition: And also; in addition; besides (which).
active_cells.example: Let's go home now. It's late, plus I'm not feeling too well.

active_cells.definition: A positive quantity.
active_cells.example: The figures show a plus.

active_cells.definition: An asset or useful addition.
active_cells.example: He is a real plus to the team.

active_cells.definition: A plus sign: +.
(abbreviation, alt-of) Abbreviation of LGBT+
(not-comparable) Being positive rather than negative or zero.
active_cells.example: −2 * −2 = +4 ("minus 2 times minus 2 equals plus four")

active_cells.definition: (not-comparable) Positive, or involving advantage.
active_cells.example: He is a plus factor.

active_cells.definition: (not-comparable) Electrically positive.
active_cells.example: A battery has both a plus pole and a minus pole.

active_cells.definition: (informal, not-comparable, postpositional) (Of a quantity) Equal to or greater than; or more; upwards.
active_cells.example: The bus can fit 60 plus kids, but we only get 48.

active_cells.definition: (informal, not-comparable) And more.
active_cells.example: Have you been to Brazil, Bhutan, or Botswana? Well, I haven't and I'm reday ^([sic]) to go ― almost anywhere interesting actually. Warm, wise world traveler seeks equally exciting, self-sufficient soul for adventures plus.

active_cells.definition: (informal) To add; to subject to addition.
active_cells.example: For him y is a unique number, like 7, but for the time being unknown — if one does the operation of 'plussing 4' one still has, as a result, a unique number even though one does not yet know what it is.

active_cells.definition: (often, followed by ‘up’) To increase in magnitude.
active_cells.example: I am doing a lot of writing here, plussing the script, adding sequences.

active_cells.definition: To improve.
active_cells.example: Coach Wooden didn't have to depend upon having the most talented players on his team because he could depend upon plussing to constantly make everyone better.

active_cells.definition: To provide critical feedback by giving suggestions for improvement rather than criticisms.

3.definition: (not-comparable) Electrically positive.

3.definition: (informal) To add; to subject to addition.
3.example: For him y is a unique number, like 7, but for the time being unknown — if one does the operation of 'plussing 4' one still has, as a result, a unique number even though one does not yet know what it is.

3.definition: (often, followed by ‘up’) To increase in magnitude.
3.example: I am doing a lot of writing here, plussing the script, adding sequences.

3.definition: To improve.
3.example: Coach Wooden didn't have to depend upon having the most talented players on his team because he could depend upon plussing to constantly make everyone better.

3.definition: To provide critical feedback by giving suggestions for improvement rather than criticisms.
3.example: The animators and directors on the receiving end of the plussing don't necessarily have to accept and incorporate the feedback, but plussing provides a method to share criticisms in a way that makes it more likely that they will.

3.definition: (sales) To sell additional related items with an original purchase.
3.example: Good will is also secured by plussing the original purchase with another article that goes appropriately with it.

3.definition: To frame in a positive light; to provide a sympathetic interpretation.
3.example: Plussing is a technique for enhancing a positive atmosphere in the session, for diminishing hostility, and for raising self-esteem.

3.definition: (social media, dated) To give a mark of approval on Google+.
3.example: How do you get others to add you or your brand to their circles? By creating and sharing useful content, commenting, plussing others' content and comments, and engaging with others on Google+.

3.definition: To increase the potency of a remedy by diluting it in water and stirring.
3.example: On hearing this, plussing was done (all medicated water of the phial was thrown away and fresh distilled was added and 10 strokes were given) on the 13th February 1974.

3.definition: To increase a correction.

active_cells.definition: A greeting (salutation) said when meeting someone or acknowledging someone’s arrival or presence.
active_cells.example: Hello, everyone.

active_cells.definition: A greeting used when answering the telephone.
active_cells.example: Hello? How may I help you?

active_cells.definition: A call for response if it is not clear if anyone is present or listening, or if a telephone conversation may have been disconnected.
active_cells.example: Hello? Is anyone there?

active_cells.definition: (colloquial) Used sarcastically to imply that the person addressed has done something the speaker considers to be foolish, or missed something that should have been obvious.
active_cells.example: You just tried to start your car with your cell phone. Hello?

active_cells.definition: (uk) An expression of puzzlement or discovery.
active_cells.example: Hello! What’s going on here?

active_cells.definition: "Hello!" or an equivalent greeting.
active_cells.example: In many new buildings, though, neighbors are venturing beyond tight-lipped hellos at the mailbox.

active_cells.definition: (transitive) To greet with "hello".
active_cells.example: She is there guarding and looking after the candy and the children generally, and she helloes and renders an exclamation that Maidie is crossing the street.

active_cells.definition: An exclamation to call attention.

3.definition: (informal) To add; to subject to addition.
3.example: For him y is a unique number, like 7, but for the time being unknown — if one does the operation of 'plussing 4' one still has, as a result, a unique number even though one does not yet know what it is.

3.definition: (often, followed by 'up') To increase in magnitude.
3.example: I am doing a lot of writing here, plussing the script, adding sequences.

3.definition: To improve.
3.example: Coach Wooden didn't have to depend upon having the most talented players on his team because he could depend upon plussing to constantly make everyone better.

3.definition: To provide critical feedback by giving suggestions for improvement rather than criticisms.
3.example: The animators and directors on the receiving end of the plussing don't necessarily have to accept and incorporate the feedback, but plussing provides a method to share criticisms in a way that makes it more likely that they will.

3.definition: (sales) To sell additional related items with an original purchase.
3.example: Good will is also secured by plussing the original purchase with another article that goes appropriately with it.

3.definition: To frame in a positive light; to provide a sympathetic interpretation.
3.example: Plussing is a technique for enhancing a positive atmosphere in the session, for diminishing hostility, and for raising self-esteem.

3.definition: (social media, dated) To give a mark of approval on Google+.
3.example: How do you get others to add you or your brand to their circles? By creating and sharing useful content, commenting, plussing others' content and comments, and engaging with others on Google+.

3.definition: To increase the potency of a remedy by diluting it in water and stirring.
3.example: On hearing this, plussing was done (all medicated water of the phial was thrown away and fresh distilled was added and 10 strokes were given) on the 13th February 1974.

3.definition: To increase a correction.
3.example: No aspheric cataract spectacle lens designer has ever given the slightest thought to this 4 to 6 diopters of over-plussing for peripheral vision which is responsible for tremendous peripheral distortion, worse peripheral swim, worse false orientation, worse magnification, severe concave curvature of field ("The floor comes up at you"), increased ring scotoma size and increase jack-in-the-box phenomenon (the "horse-blinder effect") with unsafe walking and driving.
